ranking.footnote: How to read these numbers: latency is the median of the latest probe (3 samples per site); success rate = successful requests / total requests. Data is refreshed periodically by scripts/ping_test.py, and clicking a column header sorts the table. The authenticity column shows Phase 3 probe results (scripts/authenticity_test.py); rows show — / ⏳ when no test key is configured or the fingerprint baseline is not calibrated. Click a badge to expand probe details (temperature set / self-reported ID / drift / response / timestamp). The 🇨🇳 reachable-in-China column is what this site observed from a single machine and is not an official guarantee, since cross-border networks vary by time and route. Payment methods are compiled from public information; refer to the official page. The model list was compiled from official documentation and public model lists as of 2026-08; refer to the official page.

method.title: 🧪 Testing methodology
method.lead: Every number on this site is reproducible: the method is documented here and the scripts are open source (scripts/*.py), so the data shown is the data stored. The definitions below map one-to-one onto what the pages display.

sections.title: 🧪 Test nodes (an honest statement of the single-node limitation)
items: 🇨🇳 A local machine in mainland China: the data source for the "reachable in China" column (the network where the development machine sits, not a dedicated line);
🌍 GitHub Actions runner (overseas, location scheduled by GitHub): the data source for latency / success_rate, running automatically every 6 hours;
Both viewpoints are observations: cross-border networks vary by time and route (visibility, routing and rate limiting can all change), so neither is an official guarantee.

sections.title: 📏 Sampling and decision rules
items: Each site receives a GET request to its {api_base}/models endpoint, and the median of 3 samples is reported as latency;
Success rate = share of requests with a status code below 500 and not 404;
401/403 = the service is reachable but no test key is configured (counted as success); 404 = the endpoint is misconfigured (counted as failure);
A single request times out after 10s with a concurrency cap of 8; one site timing out does not affect the others.

sections.title: ⏰ Update frequency
items: GitHub Actions cron: probes run automatically every 6 hours (UTC 02:00 / 08:00 / 14:00 / 20:00, i.e. +8 for Beijing time);
Metric changes are written back to the repository automatically and trigger a deployment;
Data files are replaced atomically (temp file + os.replace) with a .bak backup kept, so what the frontend shows is what is stored.

sections.title: 🔐 Authenticity probe (Phase 3) decision rules
items: Temperature sampling (default 0.3 / 0.7 / 1.3) plus fingerprint comparison of self-reported ID / token length / drift / repeat ratio;
When the fingerprint baseline is not calibrated (calibrated=false) the result is always reported as "⏳ Not calibrated" — never guessed;
The calibration baseline must come from an official direct channel (scripts/authenticity_test.py --calibrate);
Any challenge or appeal can be raised as a GitHub issue (include a timestamp and we can reproduce the original samples).

sections.title: 💻 Using the data directly
items: Public JSON API (snapshotted at build time): curl https://www.apiops.cloud/data/platforms.json

test.title: 🧪 Test what your API endpoint actually delivers
test.lead: Use one low-impact Quick Test to check whether an endpoint is reachable, whether the key is accepted, whether models can be discovered, and whether the selected model can complete both a chat and a streaming call. The result describes this one real observation only; it is not a permanent health check or proof of model identity.

thirdPartyTools.kicker: THIRD-PARTY TOOL · NOT PROVIDED BY THIS SITE
thirdPartyTools.title: Need a deeper authenticity check?
thirdPartyTools.lead: This page checks reachability, credentials, model discovery and the model identifier the response declares. It does not statistically fingerprint the model behind the endpoint. A separate third-party project does that by sampling answer distributions and comparing them against reference baselines.
thirdPartyTools.toolBody: Ships GPT and Claude reference baselines and reports a three-colour verdict: a strong pointer to the declared model, insufficient evidence, or a strong pointer to another candidate model. Its author states explicitly that it is not a model identity card and cannot by itself prove that a vendor is substituting models.
thirdPartyTools.onlineBody: meowllm.top (spelled meow + llm) — public HTTPS APIs only. The author states that online-version requests, including your key, are processed by Cloudflare and the service's server, and that reports are public (request URL, group and sanitised errors; the key is not included).
thirdPartyTools.localBody: Download from GitHub Releases and run it on your own machine; it is the only option for private or intranet endpoints.
thirdPartyTools.keyAdvice: Either way, use a separate, revocable key with a spending limit — the same advice the project's own README gives.
thirdPartyTools.license: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — noncommercial use only. Personal research, experiments and testing are permitted; commercial use is not licensed by that project.
thirdPartyTools.credit: Copyright 2026 chen-006 and contributors · Original project: github.com/chen-006/meow-llm-detector
thirdPartyTools.independence: This site neither provides nor endorses that project, and does not run its code or its baseline data. Our own authenticity checks (scripts/authenticity_test.py) are an independent implementation, documented on the methodology page.

probe.authorizedNoticeBody: Only test endpoints and API keys you are authorized to use. Requests go from this browser straight to the endpoint; APISpotlight does not receive or store your key and will not build a universal proxy.
probe.baseUrlHelp: HTTPS only; loopback, private networks, metadata and internal hostnames are blocked.
probe.apiKeyOptional: (optional for public endpoints; usually required for private endpoints such as BAI)
probe.apiKeyPlaceholder: Paste a dedicated, low-privilege test key
probe.apiKeyHelp: Your API key is used only from this browser to make the test request. APISpotlight does not intentionally store it; it is cleared once testing ends.
probe.discovered: Discovered {count} models. Pick one to start a Quick Test.
probe.selectModelFirst: Select a model before starting a Quick Test.
probe.footerNote: The default probe sends few requests, no concurrency, no automatic retries. CORS or provider policy may block a direct browser connection; this version does not fall back to an APISpotlight proxy and does not scan third-party endpoints automatically.
probe.verifiedByTestDetail: The specified request completed within this test window and returned a parsable response.
probe.inconclusiveDetail: Some evidence was collected, but there are discrepancies or not enough data to support a stronger conclusion.
probe.notVerifiedDetail: The request did not complete successfully, so it cannot be used to claim the model does not exist or is permanently unavailable.
probe.confidenceHigh: The request, the streaming response, latency and the returned model identity were all complete and consistent.
probe.confidenceMedium: The core request succeeded, but the model identity or one of the measurements was inconsistent or missing.
probe.confidenceLow: The request timed out or failed, or the evidence is incomplete, so this result cannot support a stronger conclusion.
probe.err401: The endpoint did not accept this credential. Enter a valid key again on this page; keys are not synced automatically from the provider console.
probe.err403: The endpoint rejected this request, which may relate to the account, plan, model permissions or a payment threshold; it does not mean the model does not exist.
probe.errTimeout: This request did not complete within the test window. Network conditions, provider load, routing or a temporary error can all produce this result.
probe.errNetwork: The browser could not complete the request, which may relate to CORS, the network connection or a temporary provider state.
probe.errQuota: The provider returned a rate-limit response; this run did not verify normal model availability.
probe.errEndpoint: The request path was not served by this endpoint; confirm this is a Base URL compatible with /models and /chat/completions.
probe.errOther: This error needs to be judged together with the HTTP status and the provider documentation.
probe.confidenceNote: Confidence describes how complete and consistent the data from this test was; it is not the probability that a model is genuine, nor a provider credit score.
probe.noModelDeclarations: Not enough model declarations in the responses to compare.
probe.verifiedItemAtLeastOne: At least one primary request returned a parsable response
probe.verifiedItemNone: No primary request returned a parsable response
probe.verifiedItemStreamingFail: The streaming response was not verified
probe.verifiedItemTtftMissing: TTFT could not be measured reliably
probe.notProvenTitle: What this test does not prove
probe.notProvenPermanent: Permanent availability or future routing behaviour
probe.notProvenHonesty: Whether a provider is honest, or the absolute identity of a model
probe.notProvenTimeout: That a single timeout means the model does not exist
probe.aboutBody1: This report records what the endpoint actually returned during this test. Relay routing, upstream models, service status and network conditions can change, so the result represents the moment it was measured.
probe.aboutBody2: Anomalous signals need repeated tests and other evidence to judge; APISpotlight will not package a single test as an unprovable "permanent certification".
probe.rerunNote: Testing again sends new low-impact real requests; endpoints that need a key require the key to be re-entered after every test. Each result has its own Test ID and timestamp.
